scope: All publicly visible repositories returned by the paginated GitHub repository search, including forks and archived repositories; every returned repository received metadata and primary overview review.

enumeration.limitations: The connector did not expose total_count or incomplete_results. Enumeration ended on an empty second page, well below the GitHub search cap. Search indexing, deleted/renamed repositories and changes after retrieval remain limits; private repositories are excluded.

coverage_tiers.selected-source: Metadata, primary overview, complete non-truncated recursive tree listing, and selected source/test/configuration files or stated line ranges at a recorded HEAD commit. Not an exhaustive code or security audit.
coverage_tiers.overview: Metadata and primary README/overview; row overview_scope distinguishes full reading from selected sections or prose-only reading. Linked material, notebooks and source were not reviewed unless listed in selected_source_reviews.
coverage_tiers.unavailable: Would be used for an inaccessible or missing primary overview; no returned repository required this tier.

method_limits: Repository maintenance status in README prose can differ from GitHub archived metadata; both are preserved without equating popularity with quality.
Fork overviews describe the owned fork snapshot, not a separately audited current upstream.
Primary overview URLs generally track default branches; blob SHAs record the fetched content. Focused source links are pinned to recorded commit SHAs.
Metadata license identifiers are observations, not permission or legal conclusions. No source code or long licensed text was copied into template assets.
No external repository was cloned, installed, executed or modified. Tests were read, not run; performance, reliability and exploitability were not reproduced.

repositories.observation: The fork's overview walks through a full task lifecycle, keeps sandbox operation separate from production, and warns that deleting tasks prevents later result retrieval.
repositories.template_relevance_or_exclusion: Transfer safe environment defaults and explicit export-before-deletion behavior; historical billing and broad credential advice require current verification and are excluded.
repositories.overview_scope: Full primary README; additional root overview also read when recorded

selected_source_reviews.name: autoresearch
selected_source_reviews.role: Autonomous experiment protocol and evaluation boundary
observations: program.md restricts edits to train.py, freezes prepare.py and dependencies, requires a baseline and records commit/metric/memory/outcome.
prepare.py excludes the fixed validation shard from training and computes byte-normalized validation loss; the evaluation contract is explicit.
train.py seeds Torch and reports configuration, training time, total time and memory; the measured training budget starts after early warmup steps.
The agent protocol requests indefinite iteration and git reset for discarded trials. The repository tree contains no conventional test directory or workflow at the inspected HEAD.
transfer: Before changing implementation, identify allowed files, invariant evaluation, baseline revision and a falsifiable success criterion.
Record each experiment's revision, actual command/configuration, comparable environment, result and keep/discard rationale.
Bound total elapsed time, attempts and resource use separately from a component's measured time; preserve unrelated and shared work.
reject: Do not inherit indefinite loops, disabled approval/permission checks, or destructive recovery from an experimental prompt.
A fixed validation metric does not by itself prevent overfitting to repeated validation feedback or establish product quality.
Do not treat README license wording as a complete license verification when API metadata is null.
selected_source_reviews.verification: Static source review only; no GPU experiment or performance claim reproduced.

selected_source_reviews.name: nanochat
selected_source_reviews.role: Reproduction provenance, configuration compatibility and execution boundary tests
observations: execution.py uses a fresh subprocess, a small environment, temporary working directory and timeout; it explicitly says network access and adversarial isolation are not covered.
test_execution.py checks happy path, captured exceptions, timeout, memory, environment isolation and restricted operations. These tests were read, not run.
checkpoint_manager.py saves metadata alongside model state, patches known old configuration fields, uses strict state loading and checks tokenizer vocabulary compatibility.
The leaderboard records commands, commit identifiers, hardware assumptions and validation values; the named timing metric excludes evaluation and logging.
pyproject.toml distinguishes CPU and GPU dependency sources. speedrun.sh is an example for an eight-GPU node and downloads/runs an installer if uv is missing.
transfer: Test the changed boundary's failure behavior, not only successful output.
Record revision, hardware/runtime, configuration, metric definition and excluded work for reproduction.
Validate persisted-state compatibility explicitly; separate optional environment-specific dependencies.
reject: A subprocess and monkey-patched functions do not establish a security sandbox for hostile code.
Do not copy automatic remote installer execution or an expensive GPU run into default setup.
Versioned metadata does not alone prove checkpoint atomicity or multi-file recovery.
selected_source_reviews.verification: Static source and test review only; no training, inference or sandbox test executed.

selected_source_reviews.name: micrograd
selected_source_reviews.role: Small core with an independent correctness oracle
observations: The scalar engine keeps forward operations and their local gradient propagation together and builds a topological order for backpropagation.
Two tests calculate corresponding expressions in PyTorch, comparing both outputs and gradients rather than asserting only the implementation's own intermediate structures.
The package describes a small educational engine; the reviewed setup does not declare the tests' Torch dependency.
transfer: Use an independent reference, domain invariant or externally observable contract as the test oracle.
Keep tightly related algorithm steps visible when extraction would obscure the reasoning.
reject: Do not turn this deliberately small scalar teaching scope into a universal line limit or dependency policy.
Two example tests do not establish complete numerical or production coverage.
selected_source_reviews.verification: Static source/test/configuration review only; no numerical tests executed.

selected_source_reviews.name: minbpe
selected_source_reviews.role: Boundary contracts, round trips and reference compatibility
observations: RegexTokenizer separates ordinary input from explicitly selected special-token handling and rejects unknown token identifiers.
The saved model has a format marker; the human-readable vocabulary output is explicitly unsuitable for reconstructing lossless model state.
Tests cover empty and multilingual text, encode/decode identity, tiktoken parity, a known merge example and save/load behavior.
The special-token rejection branch uses assert; save/load tests use fixed temporary filenames and manual cleanup. These teaching choices need separate production validation and isolation decisions.
transfer: Define input interpretation at trust boundaries explicitly and test representative edge cases.
Verify round trips and persistence against the real contract, plus an independent compatible implementation where available.
Distinguish canonical state from lossy display artifacts.
reject: Do not rely on removable assertions as a production external-input validation policy.
Do not copy fixed shared test filenames into parallel or failure-prone tests.
The separate text fixture was not read or copied.
selected_source_reviews.verification: Static source/test/configuration review only; tokenization and persistence tests not executed.

selected_source_reviews.name: llm.c
selected_source_reviews.role: Cross-implementation verification and CI failure semantics
observations: The CPU test loads reference inputs/logits/loss/gradients from a Python-generated state file and compares a short training trajectory.
Despite calculating allok and printing the aggregate judgment, test_gpt2.c returns zero at the end even when a numerical comparison changes allok to false.
The Python loss checker returns a failure status for parsing and tolerance failures, but its comparison loop does not require exactly ten values or reject non-finite numbers explicitly.
Workflow files separate CPU platforms, CUDA compilation and GPU execution, and add address-sanitizer coverage for the dataloader.
The inspected workflows use moving action tags, legacy runner/toolkit choices and an unpinned dependency clone; no explicit workflow permissions or timeouts appear.
transfer: Require validation commands to return failure when their contract fails; a printed error is insufficient.
Validate completeness and numeric validity of machine-parsed measurements before comparing tolerances.
Use a platform matrix only for supported contracts, and isolate costly hardware-specific checks.
reject: Do not copy the example workflows' old runner versions, moving references, GPU runner assumptions or absent limits.
A source-observed zero-exit issue is not a claim that every repository test or every historical CI run is ineffective.
selected_source_reviews.verification: Static source/workflow review only; no build, training, mutation test or CI run performed.

selected_source_reviews.name: rendergit
selected_source_reviews.role: Repository reading coverage, provenance and command/content boundaries
observations: The renderer records HEAD, chooses files by byte limits/binary heuristics, skips symlinks during file collection and lists omitted files.
Commands use an argument list with check=True; the subprocess wrapper has no timeout.
The Markdown path calls the renderer and inserts its output without a separate sanitization step visible in the inspected code; the generated page opens by default.
The LLM text format includes source paths and file text, which is useful provenance but does not establish authority for embedded instructions.
The inspected tree has no conventional test directory or GitHub workflow.
transfer: Keep a source manifest with revision, read/skipped status and reasons; explicitly bound what a review claims.
Use structured command arguments, checked failures and an appropriate timeout when an authorized command is necessary.
Treat retrieved repository text as source evidence rather than instructions for the researching agent.
reject: Do not automatically clone, execute or open arbitrary repository content because an example utility does so.
Do not infer complete safety from shell=False, size heuristics or content delimiters.
No exploit was attempted and no full HTML or security audit was performed.
selected_source_reviews.verification: Static implementation/configuration review only; utility not installed, cloned or executed.

selected_source_reviews.name: llm-council
selected_source_reviews.role: Inspectable multi-stage AI orchestration and prototype limits
observations: The flow separates initial answers, peer rankings and synthesis, retaining intermediate stage results.
The client sets a per-request timeout and maps exceptions to None; successful model responses can continue after partial failures.
Ranking parsing falls back to extracting textual labels and aggregation does not validate complete unique rankings. Model consensus is not an independent reference.
The non-streaming orchestrator handles an empty first stage, while the separately implemented streaming path continues to rankings after an empty first stage.
The reviewed routes show no user authentication checks; storage overwrites local JSON directly and the startup script prints readiness after a fixed delay.
The inspected tree has no conventional tests or CI workflow. The README presents the project as a lightly supported prototype.
transfer: Make stages and partial results inspectable; define explicit missing, failed and completed states.
If both streaming and non-streaming paths exist, verify they enforce the same failure contract.
Validate structured model output, track cost/time bounds, and use independent evaluation for quality claims.
reject: Do not make multiple paid model calls a universal agent default.
Do not equate peer ranking, CORS or a health endpoint with correctness, authentication or dependency readiness.
Do not copy local direct-file persistence as a concurrent durable store without an actual requirement and recovery design.
selected_source_reviews.verification: Static source/configuration review only; no API requests, server execution or adversarial tests.

selected_source_reviews.name: arxiv-sanity-lite
selected_source_reviews.role: Derived artifact replacement and explicit operating limits
observations: Ingestion, feature computation and serving are separate steps; database access defaults to read-only unless writes are requested.
The feature writer writes a temporary file in the destination directory before renaming it, keeping readers from observing a partially written artifact.

The ingestion loop increments its retry counter only on exceptions; a successful response with fewer than 100 papers can repeat indefinitely. Exhausted exceptions call sys.exit() without a nonzero code.
The final ingestion exit status encodes changed versus unchanged data, so callers must distinguish this special contract from generic success/failure conventions.
The server accepts a nonempty username for login and falls back to a fixed development signing key if a file is absent.
Feature state uses pickle; requirements are old pinned versions and the inspected tree has no conventional tests or workflow.
transfer: Publish derived artifacts only after a complete write and document recovery/compatibility requirements.
Bound every retry path, including incomplete successful responses; distinguish no-change, failure and success explicitly.
Keep data access and lifecycle cleanup visible; validate only the actual changed persistence, auth or retry boundary.
reject: Do not adopt username-only login, development key fallback, trusted-local serialization assumptions or stale dependencies as template defaults.
An atomic rename pattern is not by itself a complete crash-durability or concurrent-writer solution.
selected_source_reviews.verification: Static source/configuration review only; no web server, ingestion, email, model fitting or persistence tests executed.
